text:
Devin: heads-up — canary is showing a ~30% token/sec regression after today's runtime merge (sha: 3a5f9b2). rolling back disabled but we held the rollout.
build-bot: CI summary: https://ci.redwood.example/12345 — perf tests (tokensec) show drop from 3200 -> 2200 on ctb workload, p95 latency +120ms. logs attached.
Mara: ack. which area did that merge touch? scheduler or kernel routing?
Devin: kernel routing + prefetch heuristics. main change tried to prefer unified-copy kernel for long-context flows but fallback path changed ordering.
Lee: did a quick perf profile on the canary machine (g.prof snapshot):
```
# pprof summary
rocks: memcpy spikes on kernel_fallback() path
ctb_scheduler::dispatch -> kernel_select -> fallback_unified_copy
self  48%  48%  memcpy
```
Seems memcpy volume up, more memcopies per token.
Nora: interesting — is it falling back to a memcpy-heavy path instead of the optimized memmove-less kernel?
Devin: yeah. local bisect pointed at commit 6f21d4 which adjusted the kernel preference table and TTL for KV prefetch.
Mara: can you paste the kernel selection snippet? maybe the heuristic misclassifies sequence length distribution.
Devin: here is the relevant logic we changed:
```
if (seq_len > threshold || kv_prefetch_enabled) {
  prefer_unified_copy = true;
} else {
  prefer_unified_copy = false;
}
// fallback: if mem_usage_high -> revert to memcpy-safe kernel
```
Looks innocent but the TTL change means many short requests hit the path as if they were long due to stale prefetch metadata.
Lee: I profiled per-request kernel choice counts: unified-copy chosen 3x more often, but average memcpy per call also increased -> indicates unified-copy falling back mid-exec causing double-copy.
Mara: could we toggle the env flag to force the old kernel ordering for canary while we bisect?
Nora: +1. opsbot, can you set rollout.hold and set RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=legacy for the canary pool?
opsbot: rollout.hold applied to canary. Setting RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=legacy on pool "canary-ctb-1".
build-bot: opened revert PR: https://git.redwood/reverts/PR-6789 — includes revert of kernel-pref change and the prefetch TTL tweak. CI for revert started.
Devin: trying a tighter bisect range now; early indicator points to the combination of TTL increase + routing table reorder is the root cause (TTL caused stale prefetch tags; reorder made fallback path more likely).
Mara: if revert CI is green, we should hold and roll back the merge. if revert CI fails, plan B = patch to guard fallback so unified-copy doesn't attempt double-copy on small buffers.
Lee: quick mitigation we tested locally: reduce prefetch TTL to previous value and add a fast-path check `if (buffer_len < small_threshold) use_legacy_kernel()` — that dropped memcpy time 40% in local sim.
Nora: do we want to ship patch or revert? Devops preference?
opsbot: revert PR passed unit tests but perf CI still running (ETA ~7m).
Devin: I'm leaning revert then follow up with targeted TTL + selection guard in a follow-up PR with tests that assert memcpy counts.
Mara: agreed. please record regression details in the incident tracker and tag eng-runtime. Also add a profiling check to the perf CI to catch memcopy deltas.
Lee: will add pprof-based assertion (memcpy time delta < 5%) to perf CI.
Nora: thanks for the quick triage. once revert lands we'll re-run long-run load and verify KV hit patterns.
Devin: final note — this one felt subtle because the scheduler heuristics + KV metadata TTL interacted nonlinearly; adding more unit tests for interaction coverage will help. :thumbsup:
Mara: nice work team. keep updates here. :eyes:
